problem: The archived reproductive-success date fields contain numeric 0, numeric 999, blank cells and NULL-like strings in addition to plausible day-of-season values. The frozen contract defined eligibility and success using observed versus nonobserved event dates but did not enumerate archive sentinel encodings.

evidence_opened_before_repair.observed_pattern: Plausible event dates are positive day-of-season values; 0 and 999 occur in positions incompatible with literal event dates. Some rows with lay date 0 have later hatch/creche dates, so 0 cannot be treated as evidence of no egg.

frozen_resolution.observed_event_date: A finite integer from 1 through 998 inclusive.
frozen_resolution.primary_eligible_nest: At least one Egg 1 Lay Date or Egg 2 Lay Date is an observed event date under the rule above.
frozen_resolution.primary_success: At least one Chick 1 Creche Date or Chick 2 Creche Date is an observed event date under the rule above.
frozen_resolution.hatch_sensitivity_success: At least one Chick 1 Hatch Date or Chick 2 Hatch Date is an observed event date under the rule above.

rationale: The primary endpoint uses only whether the relevant event date was recorded. Restricting event dates to 1-998 excludes archive sentinels without using any colony-level association with future growth.
unchanged: minimum 5 eligible monitored nests per colony-season
prior-size control and colony fixed effects
minimum-information gate and all decision rules
claim_boundary: Rows whose laying dates are unobserved are excluded from the primary denominator even if later hatch or creche events are recorded.
This conservative rule may reduce information but may not be relaxed after the information count is known.
No 0 or 999 value is interpreted as a biological event date.
